introduction: In the 'Computer Knowledge' section of competitive exams (SSC, Railways, Police), Primary Memory is arguably the most frequently tested topic. At this foundational level, we focus on understanding the main memory that interacts directly with the CPU, and its two fundamental pillars: RAM and ROM.

core_concepts.title: What is Primary Memory?
core_concepts.description: Also known as 'Main Memory' or 'Internal Memory'. It is the memory that the CPU (processor) can access directly. Any program, app, or file must first be loaded into Primary Memory before the CPU can process it.

core_concepts.title: RAM (Random Access Memory)
core_concepts.description: This is the computer's 'Working Memory'. When you open a document or launch a game, it loads into RAM. It is 'Volatile', meaning it is temporary—if the power goes out, everything stored in RAM is instantly erased.

core_concepts.title: ROM (Read Only Memory)
core_concepts.description: This is the computer's 'Permanent Memory'. It contains the essential startup instructions (booting process) embedded by the manufacturer. You can only 'read' from it, not write over it. It is 'Non-Volatile', meaning it retains data even when the power is turned off.

core_concepts.title: Volatile vs. Non-Volatile
core_concepts.description: A critical distinction for exams. Volatile means data is lost when power is disconnected (e.g., RAM). Non-Volatile means data is permanently saved regardless of power (e.g., ROM).

important_entities.name: RAM
important_entities.significance: The amount of RAM (e.g., 8GB, 16GB) directly determines how many applications a computer can run simultaneously (Multitasking) without lagging.

important_entities.name: ROM
important_entities.significance: Stores the BIOS (Basic Input/Output System) which is crucial for waking up the computer hardware when you press the power button.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: The Hard Disk is NOT Primary Memory
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A very common trap! Aspirants often assume the Hard Disk Drive (HDD) or SSD is main memory because it stores the OS. Remember, the Hard Disk is 'Secondary Memory'. Primary Memory strictly refers to RAM, ROM, and Cache.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Associate the 'A' in RAM with 'Away' (data runs Away when power is off). Associate the 'O' in ROM with 'Original/Ongoing' (data is Original and permanent).

exam_strategy_tips: Direct questions like 'Which of the following is a volatile memory?' are guaranteed in Tier-1 exams. Always map Volatile to RAM immediately.
